text: Chewing-insect pests: Ladybird/leaf beetle (សត្វល្អិត lady bugs, actually a leaf-eating beetle in this context) — chews large holes in leaves starting shortly after transplanting, can prevent seedling establishment; controlled by repeated plowing, removing weed hosts, and chemicals Thiamethoxam, Acetameprid, Imidacloprid, Acephate, Lambda-Cyhalothrin, or soil-applied Dinotefuran/Fipronil around the base before planting. Armyworm — caterpillars that skeletonize leaves in groups; controlled by egg-mass removal, field sanitation, and Indoxacarb, Emamectin Benzoate, Chlorantraniliprole, Fipronil, Bacillus thuringiensis, Neem oil. Leaf folder — caterpillar that folds/webs leaves and feeds inside, mainly damages young plants; same chemical options as armyworm plus Abamectin. Leaf miner — small fly larvae tunneling visible squiggly mines inside leaf tissue; controlled by removing/destroying mined leaves and Abamectin, Emamectin Benzoate, Lambda-Cyhalothrin, Acetamiprid.
